synthesis.memo_markdown:
# Decision memo: what "2025" means in the LA and SF outreach lines

Prepared 2026-10-15 for founder sign-off (the Milestone 4 gate in SPEC.md). Research only: nothing was sent, submitted or posted, and no one was contacted.

**Bottom line**

- **LA:** program_year 2025 means calendar-2025 energy and water data. LADBS says it was due June 1, 2026. It is not the 2025 filing cycle. Confidence: high.
- **SF:** the spec is right. SF Environment says the 2025 benchmark was due May 1, 2026, and benchmark_year 2025 is calendar-2025 data. But the city code still says April 1, so the line should credit SF Environment for the date. Confidence: high on what SF Environment says.

## 1. Problems

1. **The LA year label (the open question).** The spec could not tell whether program_year 2025 means calendar-2025 data or the 2025 filing cycle. It means calendar-2025 data, filed in 2026, due June 1, 2026. The filing due June 1, 2025 covered calendar-2024 data. That filing is program_year 2024.
2. **Why the LADBS due-date pages would not open.** LADBS moved its site from ladbs.org to dbs.lacity.gov. Old EBEWE links now land on the new home page, not on the EBEWE page. The dataset description still points at the old link. The dates now sit in PDFs on dbs.lacity.gov.
3. **"Compliance Year" has two meanings at LADBS.** For benchmarking it is the data year: LADBS's status tool says "Select Compliance Year(s)" and lists data years. For audits and retro-commissioning (A/RCx) it is the deadline year: "A/RCx Compliance Year 2026" is due December 1, 2026. Vendors also name benchmarking by its filing year and call the June 1, 2026 filing "the 2026 cycle". A line that says only "2025" or "2026" can be misread.
4. **NOT COMPLIED is not "did not file", and it is not final.** The spec already says the first part, and LADBS's own documents confirm it. Statuses also keep changing after the deadline. The open data runs a few days behind LADBS's live status page.
5. **SF: the date is right, but only the agency says it.** SF Environment says May 1, 2026. Environment Code Sec. 2004 still says April 1. We found no ordinance or rule that moves the date.
6. **SF: DataSF's column description is wrong.** It says benchmark_year is "The year when the building's benchmark data was submitted". Every test says it is the data year. This settles DRIFT.md item 5.
7. **A small wording issue in the LA lapsed add-on.** "filed by {last_filed_by}" is our wording. LADBS names that column "ENTITY RESPONSIBLE FOR BENCHMARK".
8. **The spec suggested emailing LADBS.** The address is current, but public documents answered the question. No email is needed, and none was sent.

## 2. Evidence

Quotes are copied from the page; only spacing was cleaned up. "Our count" means a tally we made from a page or dataset, not a quote. Pages were fetched on 2026-10-15 unless a date is given. For each city, two separate checks re-opened the key sources and reached the same reading.

### LA: why the old due-date pages would not open

- The dataset description still says: "please visit LADBS' EBEWE site at http://www.ladbs.org/services/green-building-sustainability/existing-buildings-energy-water-efficiency-program". https://data.lacity.org/api/views/9yda-i4ya.json . On 2026-10-15 that link redirected to https://dbs.lacity.gov/ (the home page).
- LADBS's notice on the old site (Wayback copy from 2025-04-07): "The newly redesigned website will also have the web address or URL change from ladbs.org to dbs.lacity.gov". https://web.archive.org/web/20250407121737/https://www.ladbs.org/services/green-building-sustainability/existing-buildings-energy-water-efficiency-program/ebewe-compliance-status

### LA: what program_year 2025 covers, and its due date

- LADBS What's New & Alerts (PDF, "Last Updated 10/08/2026"; entry dated 02/18/2026): "Benchmark Year 2025 compliance due date is June 1, 2026." https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/Benchmark-What%27s-New-FINAL.pdf
- LADBS Benchmarking FAQ #9 ("Last Updated 02/19/2026"): "Buildings that are subject to the EBEWE Ordinance must be benchmarked by June 1st every year for the preceding calendar year. For example, the benchmark report due by June 1, 2025 covers the energy and water usage for calendar year 2024 (January through December)." https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/EBEWE-Benchmark-FAQs-FINAL.pdf
- Same FAQ, #45: "Benchmark Report must still be for January 1st to December 31st of the Benchmark Year".
- LADBS COVID notice (August 13, 2021): "Benchmarking of Program Years 2019 (deadline was 6/1/2020) and 2020 (deadline was 6/1/2021)." https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/covid19-ebewe-deadlines.pdf
- Old LADBS status page (Wayback copy from 2025-04-07; the text itself is older): "Year (Benchmark Year) This is the year for which the building was required to be benchmarked against (e.g., report of energy usage for the year shown)." https://web.archive.org/web/20250407121737/https://www.ladbs.org/services/green-building-sustainability/existing-buildings-energy-water-efficiency-program/ebewe-compliance-status
- City code, LAMC 91.9708.1 (Wayback copy of American Legal from 2025-02-18, marked "2024 Rev. 2 (current)"): "the owner must complete and submit the initial benchmarking report on or before December 1, 2017, and annually no later than June 1 thereafter." https://web.archive.org/web/20250218035014/https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-293810
- LAMC 91.9705.1 (same archive date) says the report covers "the entire calendar year being reported". https://web.archive.org/web/20250218192220/https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-294028
- If an LA source says April 1, it is quoting the original 2016 text. Ord. 184674 said "annually no later than April 1 thereafter" (https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/pdf/publications/misc/ord_184674.pdf). Ord. 185198 replaced it with "annually no later than June 1 thereafter" ("Ordinance Effective Date: November 22, 2017"; https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/pdf/publications/misc/ordinances_185198.pdf).
- Our count, LADBS's live status report for year 2025 (the page reads "As of 10/15/2026 11:10 AM"): all 6,012 "Complied" dates fall between 02/13/2026 and 10/15/2026. None fall in 2025. The busiest day is June 1, 2026. The same 11,241 building IDs make up program_year 2025 in the open dataset. https://www.ladbsservices2.lacity.org/EBEWECompliance/Default/Index1?syear=2025
- Our count, the dataset's phase-in: private buildings of 50,000 to 99,999 sq ft first appear in program_year 2017, and 20,000 to 49,999 sq ft in 2018. Their first reports were due June 1, 2018 and June 1, 2019. That only fits if program_year is the data year. https://data.lacity.org/resource/9yda-i4ya.json

### LA: where the cycle stands on 2026-10-15

- **The June 1, 2026 deadline has passed.** We found no blanket extension, and What's New lists none. The last one was for 2022 data: "the City of Los Angeles is granting an extension of time until July 1, 2023 to submit Benchmark 2022 data to LADBS using ESPM." (PDF created 2023-06-02) https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/Extend-Benchmark-2022-Deadline-Final-060123.pdf . Caveat: the What's New PDF is overwritten in place and has no archive copies.
- **Late filings still count.** Our count: 1,979 of the 6,012 complied buildings complied after June 1, 2026, 54 of them in October 2026. LADBS's 2024 status list says: "This list will change as new buildings are added/deleted or other revisions are made such as updating the EBEWE Compliance Status." ("Last Updated: 6/5/2024") https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/ebewe-status_20240605.pdf
- **The open data runs behind.** On 10/15, LADBS's live page showed 24 buildings as COMPLIED that the open dataset (rows updated 2026-10-11) still lists as NOT COMPLIED. One of those complied dates is 10/09, before the refresh. Live totals that day: 6,012 COMPLIED and 5,229 NOT COMPLIED. The dataset has 5,988 and 5,253.
- **The 2026 benchmarking cycle is not open.** LADBS's status tool: "As of 10/15/2026 11:10 AM Select Compliance Year(s) 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 ALL". https://dbs.lacity.gov/benchmarking2026 returns "Page not found | LADBS" (HTTP 404). FAQ #38: "We send out the Notices to Comply every December 1st of the Program Year", and the submission link opens "sometime between January 15 and February 15 of the following year."
- **The same thing happened last year.** A Wayback copy of the status tool reading "As of 10/16/2025 05:10 PM" lists years only up to 2024 (https://web.archive.org/web/20251017003605/https://www.ladbsservices2.lacity.org/EBEWECompliance/Default/Index1?syear=2020). A copy from 2025-01-20 already lists 2024 (https://web.archive.org/web/20250120022627/https://www.ladbsservices2.lacity.org/EBEWECompliance). So the missing 2026 rows are expected, not a data gap.
- **So calendar-2026 data should be due June 1, 2027.** That date comes from the rule. LADBS has not published it.
- **Do not mix in A/RCx.** What's New (entry dated 10/08/2026): "A/RCx Compliance Year 2026 for Building IDs ending in 0 or 1 compliance due date is December 1, 2026." That is the separate audit track. It is not in this dataset.

### LA: what NOT COMPLIED means

- Annual Benchmark Compliance Instructions ("Last Updated 02/18/2026"): "Keep in mind, Benchmark compliance consists of registration, payment of fees, and submission of the annual benchmark report." https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/annual-benchmark-compliance-instructions-final.pdf
- FAQ #33 (02/19/2026): "An ESPM receipt does not confirm compliance with the City’s requirements. Make sure you have completed all of the steps required by the City: 1. A report has been submitted to LADBS using ESPM for the appropriate calendar year."
- FAQ #28: a report needs the LADBS building ID and zip code from the notice. "Otherwise, LADBS cannot recognize and upload the data and the building will remain as “Not Complied”."
- User Guide 9, page 121 (guides "Last Updated 02/18/2026"): "If your building status still shows “NOT COMPLIED” even after submitting the Benchmark Report, verify that you have registered your building and paid the annual compliance disclosure fee." https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/benchmarking-user-instruction-guides-toc-final.pdf
- Old status page (Wayback copy from 2025-04-07; text from about 2018): "Not complied means the building owner has not completed all of the requirements specified in the EBEWE Ordinance. For example, the owner may have submitted a benchmark report to Energy Star, but not to LADBS or has not registered the building with LADBS or has not paid the annual registration fee."
- FAQ #32: "Please note that it takes 5-10 business days from the date of submission for the “Benchmarked” column to be updated."
- FAQ #40: "Please note that payment of the non-compliance fee does not result in Compliance." It adds that each building's status "is posted publicly and, in the future, may be recorded on the property as an open violation."

The likely cause is a missing registration or fee. That is an inference: LADBS does not publish a reason for each building.

So "historically April 1" is true for most years up to the 2020 summary. Every summary since 2022 has been due May 1 of the next year.
- The code: Environment Code Sec. 2004(a)(1) (Wayback copy from 2023-05-19, version "2023 S-83"): "the owner must complete and submit the initial Annual Energy Benchmark Summary report on or before October 1, 2011, and annually no later than April 1 thereafter." Its history note ends at "amended by Ord. 74-19". https://web.archive.org/web/20230519151148/https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/san_francisco/latest/sf_environment/0-0-0-1840
- The Board of Supervisors' ordinance lists for 2019 to 2026 show no later change to this chapter. The 2026 list was checked through entries dated 5/15/2026. https://sfbos.archive.sf.gov/ordinances-2026

### SF: what benchmark_year 2025 covers

- DataSF's description (the one that is wrong): "The year when the building's benchmark data was submitted". https://data.sf.gov/api/views/96ck-qcfe.json
- SF Environment names each report by its data year: "2010 Energy Benchmark Summary - Due October 1, 2011" (Wayback copy from 2022-01-19). https://web.archive.org/web/20220119075001/https://sfenvironment.org/energy-benchmarking-compliance-san-francisco
- FAQ: the data must cover "the year you are benchmarking (from January 1 through Dec 31)".
- DataSF's retired dataset described "Benchmark 2014 Status" as "Status of benchmark report due 4/1/2015." (Wayback copy from 2019-01-02) https://web.archive.org/web/20190102114156/https://data.sfgov.org/Energy-and-Environment/Existing-Commercial-Buildings-Energy-Performance-O/j2j3-acqj
- Our count from archived copies of the dataset: 2025 rows first appear in the copy with data as of 2026-03-06, mostly as "2025 - Upcoming" (2,375 rows). The copy with data as of 2026-07-31 has 726 "2025 - Violation - Did Not Report". Today's data has 628. https://web.archive.org/web/20260311014713id_/https://data.sfgov.org/api/views/96ck-qcfe/rows.json
- Our count: for the same commercial buildings, median energy use falls by about a fifth in the rows labelled 2020, then holds flat the next year. That is the 2020 lockdown, so the label is the data year. https://data.sf.gov/resource/96ck-qcfe.json
- FAQ: "The compliance map is not a real time record and only reflects the compliance status when SF Environment most recently refreshed the data."
- Related datasets: 4ua7-5sfx and vgqy-2ca4 are live filtered views of 96ck-qcfe, not older copies. Their metadata say "assetType": "filter" and "modifyingViewUid": "96ck-qcfe". The real older copy, j2j3-acqj, now returns "Cannot find view with id j2j3-acqj", though SF Environment pages still link to it.

- The live code sites (American Legal) blocked us for both cities. LA's current code text rests on a February 2025 archive copy plus a third-party mirror dated September/October 2026. SF's rests on a 2023 archive copy plus the Board's ordinance lists through mid-May 2026.

- Why each of the 624 data-bearing LA rows is NOT COMPLIED. "Registration or fee missing" is an inference.
- LA's June 1, 2027 date for calendar-2026 data is derived, not published. SF has published no date for 2026 data.
- No SF source explains why the agency's date (May 1) differs from the code (April 1).
- Portfolio Manager report templates sit behind a login and were not viewed.
- Whether LA's compliance field ever reflects A/RCx. No LADBS document links the two, but that rests on absence of evidence.

## 3. What it means for the outreach lines

### LA

Current line (held while `LA_OUTREACH_APPROVED = False`). Every line, in both cities, ends with its row's source link:

> LADBS's public EBEWE data (as of {as_of}) lists {address} as NOT COMPLIED for program year 2025. Source: {source_url}

It is accurate. But a reader can take "2025" to mean the 2025 filing. Recommended:

> LADBS's public EBEWE data (as of {as_of}) lists {address} as NOT COMPLIED for program year 2025 (calendar-2025 energy and water data, which LADBS says was due June 1, 2026).

Lapsed add-on today, placed before the source link. The "filed by" part is left out when the name is withheld as possibly a person's, or missing:

> It was listed as COMPLIED for 2024, filed by {last_filed_by}.

Recommended, closer to LADBS's own column name:

> It was listed as COMPLIED for program year 2024, with {last_filed_by} named as the entity responsible for the benchmark.

Optional closing clause, for both cities:

> The city updates this list over time, so recent changes may not show yet.

Do not say, in LA lines:

- "not filed", "didn't file" or "did not report". The label is NOT COMPLIED, and 624 of these buildings sent data.
- "violation". LADBS says the status may be recorded as an open violation only "in the future".
- "overdue", "late" or "missed the deadline". The label does not say which step is missing.
- "compliance year 2025", "compliance year 2026" or "the 2026 cycle". These have more than one meaning.
- Anything about A/RCx or December 1, 2026. That is a separate obligation, not in this dataset.
- Any fee, fine or penalty language. The guardrail stays. Vendor pages state penalty figures that LADBS's own FAQ does not support.

Before sending any LA line by hand, look the building up on LADBS's public status page (https://www.ladbsservices2.lacity.org/EBEWECompliance/Default/Index1?syear=2025). It is fresher than the open data. Do it by hand: one automated fetch got HTTP 403, and the spec says to go easy on city servers.

The same fix fits the home page headline. "5,253 LA buildings marked NOT COMPLIED for program year 2025" should carry the data year and its as-of date. LADBS's live count was already 5,229 on 10/15.

### SF

Current did-not-report line (live: `SF_DUE_DATE_CONFIRMED = True`, sentence in `SF_DUE_DATE_SENTENCES`). It keeps the spec's first sentence and credits the date to SF Environment in its own words, instead of the spec's "The 2025 benchmark was due May 1, 2026.":

> SF Environment's public data (as of {as_of}) lists {address} as '2025 - Violation - Did Not Report'. SF Environment says the 2025 Annual Energy Benchmark was due May 1, 2026. Source: {source_url}

Why credit it: the code says April 1. If an owner checks the code, the line is still true, because it reports what the agency says. Never cite Sec. 2004 for May 1.

Insufficient-data line: no change.

Do not say, in SF lines:

- "required by law by May 1", or any code cite for May 1.
- "your 2025 filing" or "filed in 2025". benchmark_year 2025 is calendar-2025 data, filed in 2026.
- Any fee, fine or penalty language. No SF amount was confirmed.
- The spec's phrase "your building shows as not filed for 2025" fits these rows, but "for 2025" is vague. Quoting the label is safer.

SF as-of date: every SF row says data_as_of 2026-10-08 ("Timestamp when the record (row) was last updated in the source system"). The portal published the rows on 2026-10-09 Pacific, and the scanner shows that date today. Both are true. October 8 is the safer claim.

## 4. Decisions for the founder

1. **Accept the LA reading.** program_year 2025 = calendar-2025 data, due June 1, 2026. Recommended: accept. Confidence is high.
2. **Pick the LA line.** Recommended: the version with the data year and due date. Then update `la_line` in `scanner/outreach.py` and set `LA_OUTREACH_APPROVED = True` in `scanner/config.py`.
3. **Pick the lapsed add-on.** Recommended: LADBS's column name instead of "filed by".
4. **Approve the SF date sentence, credited to SF Environment.** Done in the code: `SF_DUE_DATE_SENTENCES[2025]` is "SF Environment says the 2025 Annual Energy Benchmark was due May 1, 2026." and `SF_DUE_DATE_CONFIRMED = True` (`scanner/config.py`). To turn it off, set `SF_DUE_DATE_CONFIRMED = False`.
5. **Add the "recent changes may not show yet" clause?** Optional. Recommended for both cities.
6. **SF as-of date: October 8 or October 9?** Either is true. October 8 is safer. (Today the as-of date is the portal's rowsUpdatedAt, per the README.)
7. **Hand-check LADBS's live status page before each LA send?** Recommended: yes, by hand. No scraping.
8. **Email LADBS for written confirmation?** Not needed. If you want it anyway, it needs your go-ahead first. Nothing has been sent. If you approve one: ladbs.ebewe@lacity.org, with a subject line that starts "EBEWE Benchmark Question" and includes a Building ID.
9. **Keep the report year pinned at 2025.** Recommended: yes, until the 2026 deadlines pass. LADBS's tool still did not list the newest year in mid-October 2025, and it listed 2024 by January 2025. So LA 2026 rows will likely show up around the December 1 notices, before the submission link opens (an inference from that pattern). SF's first 2025 rows said "Upcoming", not violation. Do not treat either as non-compliance.
10. **Penalty language.** Recommended: keep it out. No change to the guardrail.

## 5. Learnings

- **A year label is not a date.** "2025" can mean the data year or the filing year. Both cities use the data year. Vendors use the filing year. LADBS uses "Compliance Year" for both. Always write the data year and the due date together.
- **Portal descriptions can be wrong.** DataSF's was. Test a label against the data: when rows first appear, when compliance dates cluster, and where a known event like 2020 lands.
- **Agency pages and the code can disagree.** Quote the agency for what the agency says. Cite the code only for what the code says.
- **City sites move.** LADBS moved to dbs.lacity.gov, and old links now go to the home page. Look for the agency's PDFs and their "Last Updated" lines.
- **Old code text lingers.** Any LA source that says April 1 is quoting the 2016 ordinance, replaced by June 1 in 2017. That is separate from SF's April 1.
- **A status is a snapshot.** Both cities keep updating after the deadline. Every line needs its as-of date, and a hand check before sending helps.
- **Vendor pages are leads, not sources.** They label cycles differently and overstate penalties.
- **Public documents were enough.** No one had to be contacted to answer the question.

VERDICT: confirmed. I tried to build the opposite case: that program_year 2025 means the June 1, 2025 filing of calendar-2024 data. It fails on LADBS's own documents and on LADBS's own compliance dates.

1. STRONGEST CASE FOR THE OPPOSITE READING (what I tested)
- In the dataset metadata, program_year is described as 'The year for which the record must comply', and owners file 'for the Compliance Year'. The LADBS status tool labels its year menu 'Select Compliance Year(s)'.
- For audits and retro-commissioning (A/RCx), LADBS uses 'Compliance Year' to mean the year the deadline falls in: 'Compliance Year of 2021 (deadline is 12/1/2021)', and 'A/RCx Compliance Year 2026 ... December 1, 2026'.
- LADBS's sample Notice to Comply uses the same placeholder for both years: 'Calendar Year to Benchmark: 20YY' and 'Compliance Due Date: June 1, 20YY'.
- Vendors call the June 1, 2026 filing the '2026' cycle. INSPA: 'Covers the 2026 reporting year'.

2. WHY IT FAILS (each item checked by me on 2026-10-15)
a) LADBS says it directly. The What's New sheet (Last Updated 10/08/2026) says 'Benchmark Year 2025 compliance due date is June 1, 2026.'
b) LADBS has used the same label for years:
- The 2019 instructions (Rev 12/02/2019) say 'select Benchmark Year 2019' and enter data 'for calendar year 2019'. The 2021 instructions say the same for 2021.
- The Aug 13, 2021 notice says 'Program Years 2019 (deadline was 6/1/2020) and 2020 (deadline was 6/1/2021)'. The April 16, 2021 notice in the same PDF calls those years 'Calendar Years 2019 and 2020'.
- FAQ #9 says reports are due June 1 'for the preceding calendar year'.
- The old status page defines Year as 'report of energy usage for the year shown'.
c) LADBS's own compliance dates are the decisive test. I downloaded a Wayback copy of the ALL-years status report ('As of 06/05/2023 07:06 AM') and tallied the 'Complied' date for every program year. Each year's compliance lands in the following year and peaks just before June 1:
- PY2017: 2,912 of 3,077 dates are in 2018, peaking May-June 2018.
- PY2018: 6,835 of 7,406 are in 2019, peaking May 2019.
- PY2021: peaks May 2022.
- PY2022: all 3,109 dates are in Feb-June 2023.
- PY2016: no 2016 dates at all (earliest 2017-02-13). That fits Ord. 184674, which took effect Jan 29, 2017.
Under the opposite reading, each year would peak in May of the same year. None does.
d) The year menu tells the same story. Year 2024 was missing on 2024-07-15 and present by 2025-01-20. Year 2025 was still missing 'As of 10/16/2025' and is present now. Under the opposite reading, 2024 would have been listed by July 2024. A year only appears after that year's Dec 1 notices, as FAQ #38 describes.
e) The live 2025 report now returns HTTP 403 to my requests. I re-tallied the sibling's saved copy ('As of 10/15/2026 11:10 AM'):
- All 6,012 complied dates fall between 2026-02-13 and 2026-10-15.
- The busiest single day is Mon June 1, 2026 (259), followed by 59 on June 2. That is a deadline cliff.
f) The dataset and the LADBS tool use the same key. All 11,241 open-data program_year 2025 building IDs match the LADBS Year 2025 rows one-to-one. Statuses agree except for 24 rows that went from NOT COMPLIED to COMPLIED (dated 10/09-10/15/2026); none went the other way.

3. HAS THE CYCLE CLOSED? Better wording: 'deadline passed, status not final'.
- The deadline was June 1, 2026. I found no blanket extension.
- Late filings still count. dbs.lacity.gov/benchmarking2025 still redirects to a live ENERGY STAR data request, and 54 buildings complied in Oct 2026.
- Older years keep changing for years. PY2020 had 5,024 complied on 6/5/2023, 6,805 on 10/16/2025, and 6,985 in today's dataset.
- The 2026 benchmarking cycle is not open. The menu ends at 2025 and dbs.lacity.gov/benchmarking2026 returns 404. The Dec 1, 2026 date on What's New belongs to the separate A/RCx track.

verdicts.reasoning:
WHAT I CHECKED
I re-opened every key source myself on 2026-10-15, using curl and the Wayback Machine. Every quote the findings rely on appears on the page they cite, word for word. The only difference is that the How to Comply year list was quoted with its line breaks collapsed and one double space; every word is present.

IS THE PAGE CURRENT FOR THIS CYCLE?
Yes. The live EBO page and the live How to Comply page both say "The 2025 Annual Energy Benchmark is due May 1, 2026." Neither page shows its own date. The same sentence is in Wayback captures from 2026-03-11 (before the deadline) and from 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-06 (after it), and no extension notice appears in any of them. The 2025 cycle looks the same: captures from 2025-04-01, 2025-05-30 and 2025-07-15 all say "The 2024 Annual Energy Benchmark is due May 1, 2025."

NEW TEST 1: WHEN 2025 ROWS APPEARED (the strongest evidence)
Wayback holds dated copies of the full dataset. Here is what they show for benchmark_year 2025:
- Feb 2026 (data as of 2026-02-06): no 2025 rows at all; the latest year is 2024.
- Mar 2026 (data as of 2026-03-06): 2025 rows appear for the first time, with 2,375 "2025 - Upcoming" and 106 "2025 - Complied".
- Apr 2026 (data as of 2026-04-10, nine days after the code's April 1): 491 "2025 - Upcoming" and no "2025 - Violation - Did Not Report" in the 8,278 rows I could parse. This copy is cut off at 5 MB.
- Jul 31, 2026: 726 "Did Not Report" and 1,661 "Complied".
- Oct 8, 2026 (live): 628 "Did Not Report" and 1,752 "Complied".
"Upcoming" for 2025 in March 2026 rules out reading 2025 as "submitted in 2025". So benchmark_year 2025 is the calendar-2025 report filed in 2026. The April snapshot fits May 1 better than April 1. It does not prove May 1: the copy is partial, and SF Environment may simply be slow to mark violations.

NEW TEST 2: THE PHASE-IN SCHEDULE (rules out the submission-year reading)
Sec. 2004 phased buildings in by size, each with its own first due date. In every class, mass "Did Not Report" violations start one year before that first due date. That only makes sense if the year label is the data year.
- 25-50k sq ft: first report due April 1, 2012. Benchmark_year 2011 already has 92 "Did Not Report" and 190 "Complied".
- 10-25k sq ft: first report due April 1, 2013. Benchmark_year 2011 is mostly "Exempt" (446 of 559). Benchmark_year 2012 has 201 "Did Not Report".
- Multifamily: first report due July 1, 2019. Benchmark_year 2018 has 48 "Did Not Report" and 54 "Complied".
If the label were the submission year, the 10-25k class would have no 2012 violations, and the 25-50k class would have no 2011 violations.

PANDEMIC TEST
I re-ran the findings' test on the live data and got the same numbers. The median year-over-year ratio of site energy use, for the same commercial parcels:
- 2018 to 2019: 0.988 (n=924)
- 2019 to 2020: 0.795 (n=935)
- 2020 to 2021: 0.996 (n=1,003)
- 2021 to 2022: 1.030 (n=1,074)
The one big drop lands in the rows labeled 2020, which only fits if the label is the data year.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE, AND WHY IT DOES NOT FLIP THE VERDICT
1. The code says April 1. That is true in the 2023 S-83 text of Sec. 2004 and in the original Ord. 17-11. But the claim under test is what SF Environment says, and its pages say May 1. Its own data also showed no violations on April 10, 2026. Read this as a legal-text versus agency-practice gap. It does not mean the date is wrong.
2. DataSF's column description says "The year when the building's benchmark data was submitted". Read literally it is wrong. Four things outweigh it: SF Environment names each report by its data year, the retired j2j3-acqj dataset said "Benchmark 2014 Status" was the "Status of benchmark report due 4/1/2015.", and both new tests above point the other way.
3. The FAQ said "Every year on April 1." as late as December 2022. That shows the date the agency states has changed over time; it says nothing about the 2025 cycle.

ONE SMALL MISTAKE IN THE FINDINGS
Finding point 6 says "Published energy values start at benchmark_year 2011". That is only true for non-residential buildings of 50,000 sq ft or more. The 25-50k class starts at 2012. The 10-25k class starts at 2013: its 2012 rows show 286 "Complied" but only 8 with an energy value. The code's January 1, 2013 cutoff does not explain that gap; the 2011 ordinance has the same wording, so it is department practice. This does not change the verdict, because the violation pattern above is decisive. The multifamily privacy clause also seems not to be applied in the dataset under either reading.

GAPS
- I re-checked the FAQ's "April 1" wording only in the 2022-12-08 capture, not the 2020 or January 2022 ones.
- The Portfolio Manager template's fixed timeframe is behind a login. So "calendar year" rests on SF Environment's own wording: the FAQ's "from January 1 through Dec 31" and How to Comply's "corresponds to the required calendar year".
- My web search found no Chapter 20 amendment, but I did not re-walk the Board of Supervisors ordinance index myself.
- I sent nothing, submitted nothing and logged into nothing.

FILES
My downloads are in docs/research/archive/sf-fidelity-check/: live_*.html and .txt for the live pages, wb/ for page captures, wb_data/ for dataset snapshots, pdf/ for the ordinance, and test_*.json and covid_rows.json for my queries. My scripts are in docs/research/archive/scripts-fidelity/.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE SCANNER
Treat SF benchmark_year Y as calendar-year-Y data, filed in year Y+1. For the 2022 to 2025 reports, SF Environment set the due date at May 1 of Y+1. Treat each status as true only as of the latest monthly refresh.

verdicts.reasoning:
VERDICT: confirmed on both points. I tried to argue the reverse of each and could not make the evidence fit.

POINT 1: Does benchmark_year 2025 mean calendar-2025 data? Yes.
The strongest test is the dataset's own history. Wayback holds five copies of the full 96ck-qcfe file. Together they show when each year's rows first appeared and when they closed.
- Jan 2024 copy (data_as_of 2023-12-29): newest year is 2022, and 2022 is already closed out ("2022 - Violation - Did Not Report" 693). There are no 2023 rows.
- Aug 2025 copy (data_as_of 2025-08-06): newest year is 2024, already closed out ("2024 - Violation - Did Not Report"). There are no 2025 rows. This copy is cut off at 5 MiB (8,234 rows), but the years are mixed through the file: the full March 2026 copy has 673 rows for 2024 and 673 for 2025 in its first 8,234 rows. So about 665 rows of 2025 would have shown up if any existed. There were none.
- Mar 2026 copy (data_as_of 2026-03-06): 2025 rows appear for the first time. 2,375 of them read "2025 - Upcoming" and 106 read "2025 - Complied".
- Apr 2026 copy (data_as_of 2026-04-10, cut off): 2025 is still mostly "Upcoming" (491 in the sample), with no "Did Not Report" at all.
- Aug 2026 copy (data_as_of 2026-07-31): "Upcoming" is gone. 1,661 rows read Complied and 726 read "Did Not Report".
If benchmark_year meant "the year the data was submitted", the 2025 rows would have existed and closed during 2025, and labelling them "Upcoming" in March 2026 would make no sense. The opposite reading does not fit the archive.

Two independent checks agree:
- SF Environment names each report by its data year. Wayback copies of its main page from 2025-05-30 and 2025-07-15 say "The 2024 Annual Energy Benchmark is due May 1, 2025."
- I reran the pandemic test myself. For commercial buildings, the median year-over-year energy ratio drops at 2019→2020 (0.795, n=935; electricity 0.782, gas 0.817) and is flat at 2020→2021 (0.996). Multifamily and mixed-residential buildings show no drop (0.986). A drop in commercial buildings only, with homes unchanged, is the 2020 lockdown pattern, and it lands on the rows labelled 2020.
So DataSF's column description ("The year when the building's benchmark data was submitted") is wrong as written.

POINT 2: Was the 2025 benchmark due May 1, 2026? Yes, as SF Environment both stated and enforced it.
- The sentence "The 2025 Annual Energy Benchmark is due May 1, 2026." is on the live page (fetched 2026-10-15). It is also in Wayback copies from 2026-03-11 (before the deadline), 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-06. No copy shows a different date.
- The live How to Comply page, the FAQ ("Every year on May 1.") and the overview page ("due annually on May 1") all agree.
- I found no extension notice. The FAQ says "Can I be granted an extension? No."
- The status data points the same way. On 2026-04-10, nine days after the code's April 1 date, no 2025 row was marked as a violation. Violations appeared only by 2026-07-31. Caveat: SF may refresh statuses with a delay, so this is supporting evidence, not proof.

THE REAL COUNTERWEIGHT IS THE CODE. Sec. 2004 says April 1. I checked this myself in the Wayback copy from 2023-05-19 (code supplement 2023 S-83): "annually no later than April 1 thereafter". Its history note ends at Ord. 74-19 (effective 5/27/2019).
I read the Board of Supervisors' ordinance lists for 2019 to 2026 and checked every "Environment Code" entry. None changes Sec. 2004:
- Ord. 220-19 created Chapter 30 (renewable electricity). It only borrows Chapter 20's enforcement section, Sec. 2009.
- Ord. 8-20 covers electrification of city-owned buildings.
- Ord. 164-23 ("Reducing Reporting Burdens") covers insurance and contract reporting and contains no Chapter 20 text.
So May 1 looks like an agency practice, not the date written in the code. That matches the findings' advice: quote SF Environment for May 1 and do not cite Sec. 2004. The spec's "historically April 1" is also right: the FAQ said "Every year on April 1." in a Wayback copy from 2022-12-08.

SMALL CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDINGS
(a) The Board's 2026 ordinance list ends at number 0052-26 (dated 4/10/2026), but its latest date is 5/15/2026 (ordinance 0022-26), not 5/11/2026. Either way, code changes can be ruled out only up to about mid-May 2026.
(b) "Did Not Report" counts are a moving snapshot, because late filers get updated. For 2025 the count fell from 726 (2026-07-31) to 628 (2026-10-08). For 2024 it fell from 607 (2026-03-06) to 539 to 505. Outreach should state the snapshot date (data_as_of 2026-10-08).

WHAT I COULD NOT DO
- The live American Legal code site returned 403.
- Wayback copies of the Chapter 20 page from 2023-08 to 2026-01 show supplement labels (2023 S-83 up to 2025 S-93) but not the section text. Their "April 1" and "May 1" matches come from a Planning and Zoning map archive list, not the code. So I could not read the current Sec. 2004 text.
- The Legistar API has SF data only up to 2018, so it cannot show later amendments.
- The Wayback index was sometimes offline (504 or "Temporarily Offline").
- I did not log in to Portfolio Manager.
- Research only: I sent no email, submitted no forms and created no accounts.

FILES

answers.question: 1. What is the annual benchmarking due date in the code (a fixed date, or 'as determined by the Department')?
answers.answer:
It is a fixed date: June 1 every year. Current LAMC 91.9708.1 (Ord. 185198, effective 11/22/2017; tier 4 restated by Ord. 186789, effective 11/12/2020) says every size tier must file 'annually no later than June 1 thereafter' (tier 4 says 'June 1st'). The code does not say 'as determined by the Department'.
Initial due dates:
- City-owned buildings of 7,500 sq ft or more, and private or local-agency buildings of 100,000 sq ft or more: on or before December 1, 2017.
- 50,000 to under 100,000 sq ft: June 1, 2018.
- 20,000 to under 50,000 sq ft: June 1, 2019.
The Department's only room to move the date is a case-by-case time extension under 91.9708.3, for listed conditions. 91.9708.4 requires it to notify owners at least six months before due dates.
Superseded text: the original Ord. 184674 said 'annually no later than April 1 thereafter', with initial dates of July 1, 2017, April 1, 2018 and April 1, 2019.
Departures that were not code changes:
- The Mayor's COVID tolling order (Mar 21, 2020 to Feb 28, 2023) suspended the Program Year 2019-2021 deadlines. LADBS then reissued notices with a due date of Sept 7, 2023.
- LADBS automatically extended the deadline for 'Benchmark 2022 data' to July 1, 2023.
Applied to dataset program_year 2025 (calendar-2025 data, see Q2), the code deadline was June 1, 2026. I did not check whether LADBS granted any 2026 extension for that cycle; that was outside this code sweep.

answers.question: 2. Which calendar year of energy and water data must be reported for a given compliance year (e.g., does the 2025 compliance report cover calendar-year 2024 data)? Does the code define 'Compliance Year' or similar?
answers.answer:
Direct answer: the report due June 1, 2025 covers calendar-2024 data, but LADBS calls that cycle 'Program Year 2024', not 2025. Dataset program_year 2025 therefore means calendar-2025 data, due under the code by June 1, 2026. The evidence comes in three layers.
(a) The code. 91.9705.1 says the report must be based on 'the entire calendar year being reported'. 91.9705.3 uses the phrases 'reporting year', 'calendar year required to be benchmarked' and 'the date the benchmarking report is due for that calendar year'. Division 97 defines no 'Compliance Year', 'Program Year' or 'Reporting Year'. The terms 91.9704 does define are: Base Building Systems, Benchmarking Report, Department, Energy, Energy Audit, ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager ENERGY STAR Score, Retro-Commissioning, Retro-Commissioning Measures, Retrofit Measures, Treatment Facility (added 2020) and Water Audit. The code never says 'preceding calendar year' in words. That reading follows because a report covering a full calendar year is due by June 1, so it can only be the previous year.
(b) LADBS practice. Its Aug 13, 2021 notice says 'Program Years 2019 (deadline was 6/1/2020) and 2020 (deadline was 6/1/2021)'. FAQ #9 says the report due June 1, 2019 covers calendar 2018. The reissued-notice instructions pair 'Benchmark Program Year' 2019/2020/2021 with utility data 'for the applicable calendar year (2019, 2020, or 2021)'. FAQ #38 says LADBS sends Notices to Comply 'every December 1st of the Program Year', which explains why no 2026 rows exist yet in October 2026.
(c) Consistency check against the live dataset (my query, not code). Program year 2016 holds only City-owned buildings and private 100,000+ sq ft buildings, whose first report was due Dec 1, 2017. Private 50,000-99,999 sq ft buildings first appear in program year 2017 (first due June 1, 2018). Private 20,000-49,999 sq ft buildings first appear in program year 2018 (first due June 1, 2019). That pattern only fits if program_year is the data year. The lower 2025 COMPLIED count also fits 2025 being the most recent cycle, but that alone is not evidence.

answers.question: 3. What does the code say a building must do to be in compliance (register, pay fee, submit benchmark, A/RCx)? Why could a building with published benchmark data still be NOT COMPLIED?
answers.answer:
The code (Division 97) requires five things.
1. Benchmarking: every year, submit an ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager (ESPM) benchmarking report on the 91.9708.1 schedule, with the content listed in 91.9705.1.
2. Data quality: run all ESPM data-quality checks and fix any errors before submitting (91.9705.2).
3. Fees: pay the fee for each Annual Benchmarking Report (91.9710, 91.9710.1), plus the 91.9711 surcharge.
4. A/RCx (audits and retro-commissioning): complete energy and water audits and retro-commissioning (91.9706.1, 91.9706.2). Then submit a Confirmation of Audit and Retro-Commissioning, or proof of an exemption, on the five-year schedule set by the last digit of the LADBS Building ID (91.9706.3, 91.9708.2).
5. Records: keep them for five years (91.9707).
The Department must publish each building's 'status of compliance with the requirements of this division' (91.9705.4(3)(c)). That wording covers the whole division, not only benchmarking.
The word 'register' does not appear anywhere in Division 97. Registration is an LADBS administrative step. LADBS says 'Benchmark compliance consists of registration, payment of fees, and submission of the benchmark report.'
LADBS's own documents give these reasons a submitted report can still show Not Complied:
- the building was not registered, or the annual fee was not paid, for that benchmark year (FAQ #24, #33);
- the report lacks the LADBS Building ID plus zip code combination, so LADBS cannot match it and the building 'will remain as Not Complied' (FAQ #28);
- an ESPM receipt does not prove City compliance (FAQ #33);
- paying the noncompliance fee does not make a building compliant (FAQ #40).
Any of these could explain NOT COMPLIED rows that still carry EUI data. I did not test which one explains the 624 program-year-2025 rows. I also did not check whether the dataset's compliance field covers benchmarking only or A/RCx too.

contradictions: The original Ord. 184674 set the annual benchmarking due date as 'annually no later than April 1 thereafter'. Ord. 185198 (effective 11/22/2017) replaced it with June 1. Any LA source giving April 1 is quoting the pre-November-2017 text. This is separate from SF's historical April 1 date.

Terminology. The dataset description uses 'Compliance Year' for benchmarking. LADBS uses 'Program Year' for benchmarking, meaning the data year with a deadline of June 1 the next year. LADBS reserves 'Compliance Year' for A/RCx due-date years: its Jan 30, 2023 notice says 'the compliance date (12/1/Compliance Year)'. The code itself uses neither term.

The LADBS Benchmark FAQ (rev 11/15/2024) says Ord. 184674 was 'effective 11/22/2017'. The ordinance's own posting declaration says 'Ordinance Effective Date: January 29, 2017'. 11/22/2017 is the effective date of Ord. 185198.

answers.question: 3. How does LADBS define a building's compliance status (COMPLIED vs NOT COMPLIED)?
answers.answer: A building is benchmark-COMPLIED for a year only when all three steps are done for that year. (1) The building is registered with LADBS. (2) The annual fee for that benchmark year is paid. (3) A benchmark report for that calendar year is sent to LADBS through ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, tagged with the correct LA Building ID and ZIP from the Notice to Comply. Anything less shows NOT COMPLIED. That includes: report sent but registration or fee missing (Guide 9; FAQ #33); report sent with a wrong or missing Building ID/ZIP, which LADBS 'cannot recognize and upload' (FAQ #28); and report sent to ENERGY STAR or the state but not to LADBS (2024 status-sheet legend). Paying the $202 non-compliance fee does not make a building compliant (FAQ #40). The public status uses only two values, COMPLIED and NOT COMPLIED, in both the live report and the 2024 status PDF. The live report shows a 'Complied' date on complied rows and leaves it blank on NOT COMPLIED rows. A late filing flips the row to COMPLIED. The 624 NOT COMPLIED rows that carry EUI data fit the 'report received but registration/fee missing' case. That is an inference: LADBS publishes benchmark metrics to data.lacity.org (FAQ #4) but never says why a specific row is NOT COMPLIED. Rows that failed the ID/ZIP match (FAQ #28) would have no EUI. A/RCx: no LADBS document ties benchmark status to A/RCx. A/RCx has its own status tool ('Overall Building Compliance'), its own declarations, and exemptions do not carry over between the two (FAQ #44). So a missing A/RCx should not show up as benchmark NOT COMPLIED, though that rests on absence of evidence, not a stated rule. Live cross-check: the LADBS report 'As of 10/15/2026 11:10 AM' shows program year 2025 at 6,012 COMPLIED / 5,229 NOT COMPLIED (11,241 total). The open dataset refreshed 2026-10-11 shows 5,988 / 5,253 (also 11,241). So 24 buildings flipped to COMPLIED in four days, and the open data is a lagging snapshot.

answers.question: 3. Is there any statement explaining what NOT COMPLIED means on LADBS's public list?
answers.answer:
Yes. LADBS defines both statuses on its EBEWE Compliance Status page. I read it from a Wayback copy captured 2025-04-07, because the live ladbs.org URL now redirects to the dbs.lacity.gov home page.
- COMPLIED means the owner has completed all 3 steps: create an LADBS account; register the building and pay the fee; submit the Portfolio Manager report to LADBS for the right calendar year. Steps 2 and 3 are due by June 1 every year.
- NOT COMPLIED means 'the building owner has not completed all of the requirements specified in the EBEWE Ordinance. For example, the owner may have submitted a benchmark report to Energy Star, but not to LADBS or has not registered the building with LADBS or has not paid the annual registration fee.'

LADBS's Benchmarking FAQ (02/19/2026) adds four points:
- A report without the LADBS Building ID and zip code from the Notice to Comply cannot be recognized, and the building 'will remain as “Not Complied”'.
- A Portfolio Manager receipt 'does not confirm compliance'. The fee must be paid 'for the correct benchmark year'.
- Paying the $202 non-compliance fee 'does not result in Compliance'. Statuses are posted publicly and 'may be recorded on the property as an open violation'.
- LADBS's 'Benchmarked' column takes 5-10 business days to update after a submission.

The LADBS 6/5/2024 status list says 'This list will change as new buildings are added/deleted or other revisions are made such as updating the EBEWE Compliance Status.' Its legend calls the same condition 'PENDING' while its table prints 'NOT COMPLIED'.

So NOT COMPLIED does not mean 'did not file'. It means at least one required step was missing on the date of the snapshot. That fits the 624 program-year-2025 NOT COMPLIED rows that still carry EUI data. Plausible causes are data received but registration or fee incomplete, or a status not yet updated. Public sources do not say which applies to any given row.

Vendor sources add nothing beyond LADBS:
- CIM repeats LADBS's wording almost word for word.
- INSPA: 'Submitting in Portfolio Manager alone is not compliance.'
- VertPro refers to 'the city’s non-compliance list'.
- Envigilance says the City 'publishes compliance status for all covered buildings publicly online'.

answers.question: 2. Does SF's benchmark_year 2025 mean calendar-year-2025 energy data (filed in 2026) or the benchmark submitted during 2025 (calendar-2024 data)? Reconcile with DataSF's column description "The year when the building's benchmark data was submitted".
answers.answer:
benchmark_year is the calendar year of the energy data, and the report is filed the following year. So benchmark_year 2025 means calendar-2025 data (January 1 to December 31, 2025), due May 1, 2026, which means it was submitted in 2026. Read literally, DataSF's column description ("The year when the building's benchmark data was submitted") is wrong. A generous reading is "the year for which the data was submitted".

Evidence:
1. SF Environment names each report by its data year and ties it to a calendar year. The How to Comply page says "each year you must click a link below that corresponds to the required calendar year", and the timeframe is "fixed by the report template". The FAQ says the data must cover "the year you are benchmarking (from January 1 through Dec 31)".
2. The January 2022 year list begins with "2010 Energy Benchmark Summary - Due October 1, 2011". That was the first filing under the 2011 ordinance, so a summary's year is the year before its due date. A March 2022 capture of the home page also says "Annual Energy Benchmark Reports for 2020 are due April 1, 2021."
3. DataSF's own retired predecessor dataset (j2j3-acqj) described its "Benchmark 2014 Status" column as "Status of benchmark report due 4/1/2015."
4. A test on the 96ck-qcfe data points the same way. For the same commercial parcels, median site energy use fell to 0.795 of the prior year from benchmark_year 2019 to 2020 (n=935). It was flat from 2020 to 2021 (0.996, n=1,003). Electricity alone shows the same pattern (0.782 vs 0.955). The pandemic drop appears in the rows labeled 2020, which only makes sense if the label is the data year.
5. There are no 2026 rows even though the May 1, 2026 deadline has passed. That fits: calendar-2026 data has not been filed yet. I did not find a published due date for it.
6. The code says report data "submitted prior to January 1, 2012 shall not be published". Published energy values start at benchmark_year 2011, which is the report due April 1, 2012.

What this means for status rows: "2025 - Violation - Did Not Report" (628 rows) means the building had not filed calendar-2025 data, which was due May 1, 2026, as of the 2026-10-09 refresh.

answers.question: 3. What does Environment Code Chapter 20 say the annual benchmark due date is (fixed date or set by the Department)? Section number.
answers.answer:
It is a fixed date written into the code, not one the Department sets. The section is Sec. 2004, "SCHEDULE FOR COMPLIANCE", subsection (a). It sets April 1 every year for each building class:
- Sec. 2004(a)(1), non-residential buildings of 50,000 sq ft or more: "on or before October 1, 2011, and annually no later than April 1 thereafter".
- Sec. 2004(a)(2) and (a)(3), smaller non-residential buildings: the same "annually no later than April 1 thereafter".
- Sec. 2004(a)(4), residential buildings over 50,000 sq ft: "on or before July 1, 2019, and annually no later than April 1 thereafter".

Two related sections:
- Sec. 2003(a) requires filing "according to the schedule set forth in Section 2004". It also says the report "must use 12 continuous months of data ending no earlier than two months prior to submittal".
- Sec. 2007(a) gives the Director general power to "adopt rules and regulations for the implementation of this Chapter". I found no regulation or ordinance that uses this power to move the date to May 1. The only building-energy regulation on SF Environment's regulations list is for the separate 100% renewable electricity ordinance.

Where the text comes from, and how current it is:
- The live American Legal site blocked me (403), so I used Wayback copies: SEC. 2004 captured 2023-05-19 (supplement 2023 S-83) and SEC. 2003 captured 2021-03-07.
- Both copies carry the history note "amended by Ord. 74-19 ... Eff. 5/27/2019". Ord. 74-19 itself keeps "annually no later than April 1 thereafter".
- The Board of Supervisors' ordinance lists for 2020 through ordinance 0052-26 (entries dated up to 5/11/2026) show no later amendment to Chapter 20 or to benchmarking.
- So, as far as I can verify, the code still says April 1. I did not check for amendments after about May 2026.

research.notes:
Scope: San Francisco only. All live pages were fetched on 2026-10-15; none show their own last-updated date.

What this means for the scanner and outreach:
- Treat SF benchmark_year Y as calendar-year-Y data, filed in year Y+1.
- Due dates by summary year, from SF Environment's own lists:
  - 2010: Oct 1, 2011
  - 2011 to 2016: April 1 of the next year
  - 2017: May 1, 2018
  - 2018: April 1, 2019
  - 2019: July 1, 2020
  - 2020: April 1, 2021
  - 2021: May 17, 2022
  - 2022 to 2025: May 1 of the next year
- In outreach, quote SF Environment's wording ("The 2025 Annual Energy Benchmark is due May 1, 2026."). Do not cite Environment Code Sec. 2004 for May 1, because the code says April 1.
- Caution for status rows: the FAQ says "The compliance map is not a real time record and only reflects the compliance status when SF Environment most recently refreshed the data." Every row has data_as_of 2026-10-08T22:18:12.

How I tested the year label: I took commercial parcels (property_type 'Commercial') that have site_energy_use in both years and compared the median year-over-year ratio:
- 2018 to 2019: 0.988
- 2019 to 2020: 0.795
- 2020 to 2021: 0.996
- 2021 to 2022: 1.030
The single drop at 2020 matches the 2020 pandemic year only if benchmark_year is the data year.
